962f9c5523795700eb5370d2598270634267ea80: UI compatibility limits: the primary React shell does not load /ui/control.js; minimal SSR ui.layout still does.
ui.eval returns dispatched:true for emission, not execution.
ui.action returns dispatched:true for emission, not execution.
Navigation and toast events need a compatible consumer
An event subscriber alone proves neither that bridge nor a specific target.
screen.eval waits for a result through the compatibility bridge and can time out; its consumer requires window.page from the screen client, even for plain DOM code.
screen.openTab first needs screen.eval for the origin before using CDP.
UI compatibility bridge limits do not disable server-side ui.createAgent/sendToAgent effects; their optional navigation is best-effort.

For browser automation, discover the browser plugin with plugins.search({ query: "browser automation" }), then plugins.read({ name: "browser" }) and follow its prerequisites rather than guessing APIs or Chrome availability.
32b7559357172bcbc746f0a7b632d49d6200e519: A large surface left of the chat where you can put something in front of the person — a file, document or diagram.
Open a tab with `await ctx.fns.canvas.show({ kind, args, title? })`; it becomes active and the canvas opens.
When the canvas changes you get a short `Canvas` block saying what is open.
`canvas.list({})` shows the tabs; `canvas.list({ closed: true })` lists recently closed tabs with their `closedAt`.
`canvas.close({ itemId })` marks a tab closed; it is kept for 30 days.
`canvas.reopen({ itemId })` brings a closed tab back with its state.
`canvas.setState({ itemId, state })` remembers a tab's own state.
83c70082481c59d056f8c28f3cc1f3adc0ffe5ac: When the person asks to open, show or look at a file, a README, a document or a picture, put it on the canvas.
Only the canvas region refreshes; the chat, drafts and scroll stay.
Showing the same thing again just switches to its tab.
Relative paths resolve in your workspace; for another project pass an absolute path.
